key_insight: Welding parameters and seam geometry strongly influence coated-fabric joint strength, with peak joint efficiencies of 108.23% for PVC lap seams and 101.57% for PTFE seams.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing temperature, time, pressure, and joint configuration can reduce weld-seam vulnerability in membrane structures.
method: Orthogonal experiments varying welding temperature, time, and pressure.
Failure-mode, mechanical, and microstructural analysis of three weld configurations.
Strength prediction model evaluated against measured joint performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports prediction errors ≤5%; at 380°C, 80 s, and 0.5 MPa, predicted strength was 6,954.98 N with 0.89% error, while 78% of PVC lap specimens failed in the base material.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term durability or transferability of the optimal parameters across fabric grades and welding equipment.
paper_title: Influence of Welding Process Parameters on Mechanical Properties of Coated Fabric Weld Seams
